provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The constructor puts 2x2 squares of colour 2 at strictly increasing left columns, ending at the right wall. The square farthest right becomes 8, and so does every second square going left; the archived solver sorts by -x0 in the same way. The factory works out which visible direction the original east axis points to. For flip variants, reversing each row turns east into west. Each clockwise turn maps (dy,dx) to (dx,-dy). The emitted program finds the 4-connected components of palette[2] in the visible grid. It ranks them by their projection onto that direction (DY*y+DX*x) at the trailing edge, which corresponds to the original left column. It recolours the 1st, 3rd, 5th, ... square from the far end to palette[8]. Everything else is left unchanged. Colour roles are fixed as palette[2] for squares and palette[8] for the highlight. The program does not rotate, normalise or remap the grid. Squares never touch orthogonally in this domain: spacing 1 forces a row difference of at least 3, spacing 2 forces at least 2, and squares two apart are separated by at least one column. So each component is exactly one square. Squares at the grid boundary are handled with no special casing.
draft_notes.limitations: The generator gives every square a distinct left column, so squares never tie along the sweep axis. If a tie did occur outside the domain, the emitted program breaks it by the square's smallest (row, col) cell, but only for determinism; that is not a puzzle rule. Demonstrations are ignored because the colour roles come from the palette constants. The program assumes squares do not touch orthogonally, which the constructor's row and spacing constraints guarantee. No constructor defects or contradictions with the fixtures were found: all 5 train pairs and the test pair match 'recolour alternate squares starting from the rightmost'. The host's verification has not been run.
